# Design digest (auto-generated from designer returns, 2026-09-07)

Full designs are in this folder. Read them in full before synthesizing.

## D1-encyclopedist
(full: C:\Users\OMISTAJA\PsychologyReplication\_planning\designs\D1-encyclopedist.md)

**Summary:** D1 designs the wiki as an effect registry with everything else hanging off it. Entities: Effect (immutable fx_ id + mutable slug + alias table), Claim (doi_o x study_o x claim text, the FReD-to-effect bridge), Paper (normalized DOI; URL/handle scheme for the ~600 DOI-less works; md5 hash URL compatible with FORRT's Zotero API), Attempt at two grains (FLoRA pair carrying outcome+quote; nested FReD effect rows carrying statistics), Project, Author, Topic (facets: FORRT discipline + OpenAlex + curated tags, no new taxonomy), Paradigm (Cognitive Atlas vocabulary), Collection, Candidate. Computed from the FORRT files: 3,820 distinct original DOIs, 3,730 replication DOIs (7,491 papers), 4,550 (original, replication-id) pairs, 3,672 with an outcome grain. Effect-name sources overlap as: legacy 414 names, Reversals/R&R sheet 583/584 (its renamed/alternative/status columns are 100% empty), docx 361; exact union 961 -> 802 after normalization -> 749 after fuzzy ratio>=92 (59 merges to review). A 7-step deterministic merge algorithm (normalize, cluster names with discipline and DOI-disjoint guards, attach DOIs incl. Crossref resolution of the docx's 329 titles, same-DOI merge, unnamed finding stubs for every original with attempts but no name, attach attempts, compute status, apply overlays) yields ~720 named effects + ~3,100 stubs; 1,605 of 2,164 current FReD rows (629 originals) and 1,728 FLoRA-only originals have no name anywhere, so stubs are mandatory. Verified counter-example built into the algorithm: 'moral priming (cleanliness)' (Schnall 2008) must not merge with 'Moral Priming' (Mazar 2008, 70 rows) despite identical normalized names. Status vocabulary (8 values: Untested, Insufficient evidence, Replicated, Largely replicated, Contested, Largely failed, Failed, Reversed) with exact count rules over author-reported verdicts (FLoRA > FReD > legacy priority), a single-attempt qualifier, confidence tiers A-D, reproductions kept as a separate badge, and Reversed as curated-only because 4 of the first 12 numeric opposite-sign candidates are rows FORRT coded 'successful'. Dry run: median 1 attempt per original; 285 originals with >=2; by original paper: insufficient 1,358 / replicated-single 982 / failed-single 718 / failed 96 / replicated 49 / contested 25. The numerical lens (7 R-package criteria + effect-size ratio) is shown beside the status and never folded into it, with a 'lenses disagree' chip. Page types (effect, paper, attempt, project, author, topic, paradigm, collection, journal, year, queue, rules, data/API) are specified at 5 s / 30 s / 5 min depth. Curation overlay: one YAML-front-matter Markdown file per effect in curated/ (summary, aliases, claims pinning, status_override with justification, related, paradigms, textbooks, wikipedia, famous-list import, review state) plus cell-level corrections overlays forwarded to FORRT, merges.yaml, redirects; git PR flow with CI schema/ID/DOI validation, 1-vs-2 reviewer rules, preview builds, auto-changelog, and reviewer decisions stored as overlays. Worked example: the Macbeth effect (Zhong & Liljenquist 2006) with all 7 attempts, 8,600 participants, computed status Largely failed / confidence A (vs docx 'mixed'), all seven criteria computed per row (0/8 significant, 3/8 CI-consistent, 0/8 small telescopes, median ES ratio 0.00), a legacy source conflict (curatescience44) handled by the corrections overlay, and related effects derived from the data.

**Top ideas:**
- Effect registry with immutable fx_ IDs in committed registry CSVs, mutable slugs, redirect table for merges; the build refuses to re-assign an ID
- Unnamed finding stubs: every original DOI with attempts gets an effect page even without a name (~3,100), so all 2,815 FLoRA pairs land somewhere and naming becomes a visible curation queue
- Deterministic 7-step name-merge algorithm with discipline and DOI-disjoint guards (verified counter-example: Schnall 'moral priming (cleanliness)' vs Mazar 'Moral Priming' normalize identically but are different effects)
- Claims as the FReD-to-effect bridge: (doi_o, study_o, claim text) lets one effect span several originals and one original host several effects
- Attempts at two grains mirroring FORRT (FLoRA pair with outcome+quote; nested FReD effect rows with statistics), with FLoRA > FReD > legacy priority and conflicts kept visible
- 8-value status vocabulary with exact count rules, single-attempt qualifier and confidence tiers A-D; dry run shows median 1 attempt per original, so honesty about single attempts is the headline
- Reversed is curated-only: numeric opposite-sign candidates (40 rows / 30 originals) are flagged, not auto-declared, because FReD sign conventions mislabel 4 of 12
- Numerical lens computed per row from the R package's 7 criteria and shown beside the author-reported status with a 'lenses disagree' chip; never merged into the status
- Curated overlay = one YAML+Markdown file per effect plus cell-level corrections overlays (with reason, evidence, upstream ticket) applied before status computation and exported monthly in FORRT's submission template
- Docx famous-list status displayed as 'curated list (2022) said: mixed' beside the computed status, and the disagreement list between the two becomes the first curation queue for the 362 famous effects

## D2-metascientist
(full: C:\Users\OMISTAJA\PsychologyReplication\_planning\designs\D2-metascientist.md)

**Summary:** D2 (meta-scientist) specifies the computed-evidence layer of the wiki and backs every rule with numbers computed today from the real FORRT files. Units: Attempt (FReD row; use the archive file because output_FReD.xlsx has entry_id==1), Pair (FLoRA row), Effect (legacy names + Reversals + docx overlay; fallback (doi_o, study_o)), Original, Project. Re-implemented FORRT's r-conversion and all 7 R-package success criteria in Python: 1,103 tier-A attempts (r+N both sides; 94.1% agreement with FORRT's statistical_success, 87.2% with authors' reported_success). Criterion success shares range from 35.6% (consistency_ci) to 71.4% (significance_agg); on 942 attempts with all 7 defined the criteria disagree on 62.3% (unanimous success 207, unanimous failure 148) — so no single score is ever shown, only the 7-cell matrix. Shrinkage: median replication retains 37% of the original (IQR 5–95%), 19.9% flip sign, 22.4% ≥ original; median r_o .307 vs r_r .100. Predictors in FORRT data: original p ≤ .005 → 56.8% vs 26.1% for .005<p<.05 (n=512/299; inverts under the prediction-interval criterion); N-ratio gradient 67.0%→37.3% under authors' verdicts but flat under significance_r; author overlap>0 → 87.3% vs 49.3%; closeness closest tertile 58.9% vs ~34%. Base rates with three denominators (rows 45.5% / entries 40.5% / originals 44.0% successful; FLoRA pairs 41.3/35.7/22.3) because 47.3% of FReD rows sit in mega-papers (Boyce 280 rows). Per-effect random-effects meta-analysis (Fisher-z DL, sites pooled within project first, PI, I², leave-one-out stability) run on the 35 legacy named effects with k≥2: 69% of k≥3 effects have pooled CI>0 but 72.4% are below half the original and only 41.4% originals fall inside the replication PI — hence a graded status vocabulary (robust / smaller / heterogeneous / negligible / inconclusive / reversed / single attempt / author-reported only) with rule, tier mix and alternative labels attached. Conversion pitfalls enumerated as machine flags (partial eta 173/198 rows, unsigned eta/F/chi conversions = 33% of tier-A originals, nested designs 21%, 135 unparsed test-statistic strings incl. FORRT regex bugs, 'r-squared' label bug losing 42 rows, 45+125 reported-vs-recomputed significance mismatches). Visualizations: per-effect forest plot with project grouping and PI band, RP:P-style shrinkage scatter with criterion toggle, cumulative-meta evidence timeline, discipline×year small multiples with Wilson CIs and denominator toggle, 10-cell closeness fingerprint glyph, criteria disagreement heat-map, text-first status band. Site-wide pages /stats/{overview,criteria,shrinkage,predictors,by-discipline,by-year,projects,data-quality,methods} all pre-populated with the computed numbers. Pipeline modules es_convert / uncertainty / criteria / attempt_indicators / meta / status / aggregate / dq with formulas, pseudo-code, golden tests from the R vignette and a ≥.94 regression threshold. Artefacts: _planning/designs/D2-metascientist.md, _d2_compute.py, _d2_compute2.py, logs, _d2_fred_computed.pkl, _d2_effect_meta_legacy.csv.

**Top ideas:**
- Show the 7-criterion matrix per attempt and print the fact that criteria disagree on 62.3% of attempts (unanimous only 37.7%) — the disagreement is the content, never averaged into a score
- Effect verdict = random-effects pool of REPLICATIONS ONLY (Fisher-z, sites pooled within project first) reported as CI + prediction interval + tau/I² + leave-one-out stability; originals shown but excluded from pooling
- A graded status vocabulary with a 'Replicated — smaller' label, because 72% of multi-attempt effects exist with CI>0 yet at under half the original size, and only 41% of originals sit inside the replication prediction interval
- Shrinkage ratio (median 37% retained, 20% sign flips, 22% at least as large) as the headline number, with a Fisher-z difference CI and suppression when |r_o|<.05
- Three denominators on every statistic (rows / paper-pair entries / unique originals) plus a mega-report flag, since 47.3% of FReD rows come from ten mega-papers and the headline rate moves 40.5%–45.5% with the denominator
- Data tiers A/B/C/D/R stamped on every entity so 1,843 quote-only FLoRA pairs and 289 reproductions are never mixed into numeric verdicts
- A public /stats/data-quality page listing conversion losses (partial eta 173, unsigned conversions 33%, 135 unparsed test statistics, the 'r-squared' label bug, 45+125 reported-vs-recomputed p mismatches) and ours-vs-FORRT diffs
- Predictor page with FORRT-data facts for the game: p<=.005 originals replicate 56.8% vs 26.1%; author overlap 87.3% vs 49.3%; N-ratio effect vanishes under significance_r (a selection artefact) and inverts under the PI criterion
- Cumulative-meta evidence timeline per effect ('what the pooled replication evidence said at the end of each year') with curated event markers and author-report ticks
- Closeness fingerprint glyph from the 10 Brandt-recipe columns (closest tertile 58.9% success vs ~34%), honest 'not coded' hatching for the 96% of rows lacking it, and the same 10 integers as the curation/OSF-registration target

## D3-game
(full: C:\Users\OMISTAJA\PsychologyReplication\_planning\designs\D3-game.md)

**Summary:** D3 designs the 'Did it replicate?' game as a product and a forecast-data instrument. Verified prior art: FORRT's saved quiz.html is only the 80,000 Hours WordPress shell around an empty GuidedTrack program container (id 8032) — no items, no answers; the design instead copies Hoogeveen 2020's authoring rules (lay-rephrased claims, no authors/titles/quotes, stratified ~50%, description-only vs description+evidence). Computed the fair item pool from the real files: current FReD has 1,772 clear (successful/failed) effect rows, 1,757 with text+year+N, 1,408 after removing leaky blocks (JOM management 103 rows, Soto 60, 13 skewed replication papers); at the unit this design adopts — one item per original study (doi_o+study_o) — that is 693 originals with a consistent outcome (349 replicated / 344 failed), 620 per doi_o; social 228, cognitive 138, psychology 80, exp. philosophy 38, economics 36, marketing 27, JDM 25; decades 2000s 223 / 2010s 379. The original-study grain dissolves the block-leakage problem (701 vs 693 with/without the skew rule). FLoRA adds 1,799 consistent-outcome originals of which 1,188 are absent from FReD (playable only after an LLM claim-writing step; 422 have OA URLs, only 63 local abstracts, no N). The 362 famous effects give 223 binary items (113 replicated/101 not/9 reversed; 11 leaky descriptions). Legacy FReD 2.4.1 adds only 19 new originals but supplies effect names (794 matched rows), closeness, power, CIs, prereg for reveals; its Reversals sheet has no status filled. In-pool cue base rates: p<=.005 61% vs .005-.05 39%; 2015+ originals 59%; N<=50 51%; social 42% vs cognitive 61%; a text proxy for interactions is useless (48 vs 52%), so design type must be coded by the claim writer. Stats-mode fields on fair rows: p 1,339, r on both sides 554, replication N 1,405, authors' verdict quote 1,408 (100%), author_overlap 1,303. Design covers: modes (daily 10 deterministic, endless adaptive, by discipline/decade, famous, stats mode with purchasable cues whose paths are the research payload, classroom rooms, open forecasts, expert 3-way), card anatomy and item JSON with answers in a separate reveal file, probability slider + Brier points (100×(1−4B)) + calibration curve + non-multiplying streaks + Wordle-style share cards + daily-only leaderboards, fairness rules and five leakage tests (regex, entity/n-gram, hedging parity, model-guess test, crowd retirement), a Sonnet-batch claim-writing pipeline (<$10 for ~2,100 items) with review states, crowd forecasts on unreplicated effects settled by weekly FLoRA diffs and shrunk toward a transparent cue-based prior by measured crowd skill, an open forecast dataset, static-first storage with a Supabase schema (owner's org has 5 INACTIVE projects), abuse and privacy stances, UI/mobile/PWA flow, and a build plan.

**Top ideas:**
- Unit of play = one original study (doi_o+study_o), not the FReD effect row: 693 fair originals today at 50.4% base rate, and the leaky-block problem (JOM 76 identical rows, Soto) collapses to 1 item each instead of needing patches
- Stats mode as an instrument: players 'buy' cues one at a time (p-bucket, N, ES, journal, era, design, replication team) and re-forecast after each; the stored cue path measures the marginal value of every cue on thousands of items (a scaled Hoogeveen description-vs-evidence experiment)
- Crowd replicability forecasts on effects with no replication yet (from OSF Replication Recipe registrations without post-completion, PsyArXiv preprints, FORRT's 686-row backlog, most-cited never-replicated originals), auto-settled by the weekly FLoRA diff and displayed on every wiki finding page shrunk by the crowd's measured skill on settled items
- Model-guess leakage test: an LLM/classifier given only the card text must not beat ~70%; item-level flags when it is confident for a wording reason; plus hedging-parity test so replicated claims are not written more confidently than failed ones
- Onboarding teaches base rates and cues with BOTH the literature (p<=.005 74% vs 28%; interactions 20% vs 53%) and our own pool numbers (61% vs 39%; 2015+ 59%), making the gap itself a lesson about selection into replication projects
- Answers never ship in the item list: per-item reveal.json fetched after lock-in statically, or returned by a Supabase Edge Function that computes the Brier server-side for leaderboards
- Wordle-style share string (green = confident and right, yellow = hedged, red = wrong) on a deterministic daily set so shares reveal nothing and everyone compares on identical items; daily-only leaderboards ranked by mean Brier with >=10 items
- Reveal = the wiki's three lenses compacted: authors' verdict quote (available on 100% of fair items), forest strip with r_o/r_r and disagreement among FReD's seven criteria, closeness/prereg/independence, plus citation-trajectory sparkline and external market/lay forecasts where Gordon/Hoogeveen/SCORE cover the item
- Claim-writing pipeline: Sonnet batch with a strict schema (claim_plain <=30 words, claim_method with N in words, design type, IV/DV kind) over FReD description+claim_text_o or FLoRA title+abstract, review states machine/spot-checked/reviewed, daily sets use reviewed only, edits stored as overlays and exportable back to FORRT
- Open forecast dataset (CC0) with k-anonymised player hashes, cue paths and timings: one month of 1,000 daily players yields more human replication forecasts than Gordon (103) + Hoogeveen (27) combined

## D4-discovery
(full: C:\Users\OMISTAJA\PsychologyReplication\_planning\designs\D4-discovery.md)

**Summary:** D4 designs an end-to-end, measured discovery engine for replication pairs beyond FORRT. Verified facts anchor it: FLoRA holds ~120-180 unique replication DOIs per year (2021: 139), only 60-83% of FLoRA titles contain "replicat" (so title search is structurally capped and citation-graph crawling is required), FORRT's own OpenAlex route yields just 3-23 pairs/yr, FORRT's flora-validation validated_export.csv (263 rows, downloaded live) reveals their exact LLM-assisted ingest schema, and FORRT's backlog sheet has 189 uncoded replication DOIs. The unit of discovery is the FLoRA row (doi_o, doi_r, outcome, verbatim quote, quote source). Layout: a `discovery/` Python package with per-source modules (S1 OpenAlex cites-crawl of ~3,500-4,000 seed originals incl. the 362 famous effects; S2 OpenAlex per-year keyword crawl across fields 32/20/33/14/28; S3 venue feeds; S4 OSF preprints; S5 OSF registrations with Replication Recipe parsing; S6 Semantic Scholar citation contexts; S7 external lists incl. Curate Science/OpenMKT/ReplicationWiki/Transparent Replications/FORRT backlog+validated_export; Crossref metadata-only), immutable raw JSONL per source-week, rebuildable SQLite cache, git-tracked YAML decisions (one per candidate, append-only events), generated overlay CSV with provenance badges (community-added pending FORRT -> submitted -> merged upstream), export in FORRT's validated_export/FLoRA columns and datasubmission_template.xlsx, and a weekly idempotent crawl with per-source cursors, weekly FLoRA refresh dedup, a budget meter under OpenAlex's $1/day (EST $0.13/week; backfill ~$0.40), and LLM triage via Batches (~$2.25/1k candidates; strict JSON schema with per-target outcome+quote, quote-grounding verification, tiered routing, model_id/prompt_version stored). The evaluation harness comes first: recall by year vs FLoRA doi_r and pair recall, title-ceiling, precision on the labelled 125-row 2021 file + growing hard negatives, outcome replay on 1,741 abstract-sourced FLoRA rows + 263 validated_export rows, resolver accuracy, cost; offline cassettes; a gate that refuses regressions on any change to sources/prompts/scorer. Review UI lives inside the wiki (/review/ pages, local serve.py writes YAML; optional Supabase sync), plus 'open candidates' tabs on effect pages. Reverse discovery produces dated, search-logged 'no replication found as of <date>' statements and a 'most wanted' list. EST yield: 150-250 net-new replication papers/yr (300-500 pairs) plus 30-60 registrations/yr; backfill 1,500-3,000 pairs. Function signatures for every module are in the file.

**Top ideas:**
- Evaluation harness first, gate second, crawl third: recall-by-year vs pinned FLoRA doi_r, pair recall after resolution, precision on the labelled 125-row 2021 file, outcome replay on 1,741 abstract-sourced FLoRA rows + FORRT's 263-row validated_export, with offline API cassettes and a CI gate that exits non-zero on any regression from a source/prompt/scorer change
- Make the citation graph the primary primitive: OpenAlex cites:{100 seeds} + replicat* over ~3,500-4,000 seed originals (FLoRA + FReD + legacy-only 937 + the 362 famous effects) reaches the 17-40% of replications whose titles never say 'replication' and returns the (doi_o, doi_r) pair directly
- Contribute back in FORRT's own ingest schema: their live flora-validation validated_export.csv (37 columns incl. screen_categories, outcome_quote_source, doi_r_published) is what prepare_flora.qmd merges by common columns, so a CSV in that shape is a zero-friction PR; plus datasubmission_template.xlsx for effect-level numbers
- Per-target triage schema: one LLM output lists every original a multi-study paper replicates, each with resolved DOI basis (cited_seed/reference_list/text_only), study number, FLoRA-vocabulary outcome and a verbatim quote that is mechanically verified to exist in the supplied text (quote_grounding >= .98 gate)
- Git-tracked YAML decision files (one per candidate, append-only events, enum reject reasons) written by a tiny localhost serve.py behind the wiki's own /review/ pages, so reviewer decisions become both the curated overlay and the labelled training/eval set automatically
- Provenance badge lifecycle on every community row: 'Community-added, pending FORRT' -> 'Submitted <date>' -> 'In FORRT since <release>', flipped automatically by the weekly FLoRA refresh (mark_merged_upstream), closing the contribution loop visibly
- Reverse discovery as a falsifiable claim: per-effect search logs (citing works scanned, S2 sentences, registrations, preprints) rendered as 'No replication found as of <date>' with next_check dates and a 'most wanted' list of most-cited never-replicated originals
- Mine FORRT's own unused assets: the 189 replication DOIs in the 2.4.1 'Additional Studies to be added' backlog, the 62 genuine non-FLoRA 2021 harvester finds, and validated_export as day-one queue material and outcome gold labels
- OSF Registrations as a separate evidence tier (FORRT excludes registrations): Replication Recipe item1-37 parsing ported from rr_scraper_links.R, 'registered YYYY, no report found as of <date>' file-drawer signal after 3 years, and student/CREP/Expra replications surfaced on effect pages
- Weekly idempotent crawl keyed by (source, week) with per-seed cited_by_count cursors, 30-day OpenAlex backfill window, preprint<->article collapse via Crossref relation/OSF attributes.doi, a budget meter using meta.cost_usd (EST $0.13/week keyless), one lock file per process, and a weekly 'misses' log of pairs FORRT added that we had not surfaced

## D5-architect
(full: C:\Users\OMISTAJA\PsychologyReplication\_planning\designs\D5-architect.md)

**Summary:** D5 architecture design written to C:\Users\OMISTAJA\PsychologyReplication\_planning\designs\D5-architect.md. Stack: Python 3.13 pipeline package (pandas for ingest, pydantic v2 contracts exported to JSON Schema and then TS types, DuckDB + Parquet for joins/integrity SQL/notebooks, uv lockfile; all libraries verified installed) and Astro 7 static site with Preact islands, Pagefind full-text over effect/project/topic pages plus lazy sharded MiniSearch entity typeahead, build-time SVG charts written as Preact components (one hydrated explorer island), hosted on GitHub Pages because the estimated ~18-22k output files exceed Cloudflare Pages' 20,000-file cap; Supabase deferred to Phase 3 for crowd guesses only, never on the read path. Four-layer repo (data/raw immutable with sha256 MANIFEST; data/cache API caches; data/curated human YAML/CSV incl. append-only id ledgers and review-decision JSONL; data/build generated and gitignored except a committed SUMMARY.json baseline), pipeline/ CLI (fetch, normalize, merge-legacy, registry, score, enrich, game-items, export, validate, build, diff, docs, migrate, discover, review), site/, docs/, archive/, notebooks/, tests/, .github/workflows (ci, weekly refresh PR, deploy + data Release, weekly discovery PR). Contracts defined for Paper, OriginalStudy, Attempt, ReplicationPair, Effect, Project, Person, Topic, GameItem, Candidate, Bundle with a universal Provenance/Label wrapper (source, method, confidence, review_state). ID rules: FORRT-compatible DOI normalization and md5 hash3, readable collision-guarded paper slugs, an append-only effect-id ledger (named effects readable, unnamed FReD groups hashed, FLoRA-only originals do not create effects, LLM names are machine aliases), content-derived pair/attempt ids that let legacy 2.4.1 rows, fred_id, fred_id_old and COS entry/effect ids coexist inside Attempt.ids. 15 tests (schema freshness, ids, DuckDB referential integrity, count baselines that fail on >1% drops, legacy merge accounting summing to 4,659, R-package port vs COS oracle, vocab completeness, provenance, orphan pages/links, page budget, secrets, root allowlist, doc numbers, external links, game items). Complete migration table for every root file/folder, output/, cogatlas/, openalex_analysis/, logs/, wiki/ and data/raw/forrt with a verified 52-file secrets scrub list (51 .py + CATEGORIZATION_IMPROVEMENT_PLAN.md) and a TRASH-then-delete-after-30-days protocol, executed by a `pipeline migrate` command that refuses unplanned files. Docs set with generated data model/sources tables and placeholder-rendered numbers, 14 mechanically enforced anti-rot rules, and Phase-1 module list with function signatures.

**Top ideas:**
- Root allowlist test: the repo root may contain only the named entries; any stray script/csv/json fails CI, so the current mess is structurally impossible to recreate
- Append-only effect-id ledger (data/curated/registry/effect_ids.csv): ids assigned once by key, merges recorded as merged_into with redirects, never renumbered; unnamed FReD groups get hashed ids, FLoRA-only originals do not create effects
- Committed SUMMARY.json baseline + test_counts: any table dropping >1% or any source row count dropping fails unless --accept-baseline plus a CHANGELOG-DATA line accompany it
- Legacy merge accounting test: matched + kept + explicitly excluded legacy rows must equal 4,659, and closeness/power/CI fields may only carry source=fred_legacy_2.4.1 provenance
- COS archive as test oracle for the R-package port: recomputed r_o/r_r must match the 733 precomputed rows within 1e-3 and significance_r agreement with statistical_success on 901 rows is floored
- Docs that cannot lie: numbers in docs are {{counts.*}} placeholders rendered from SUMMARY.json, literal numbers must sit in verified blocks re-checked by a test
- GitHub Pages over Cloudflare Pages, decided by arithmetic: ~18-22k output files (papers + effects + Pagefind fragments + FORRT-compatible hash3 JSON) exceeds Cloudflare's 20,000-file cap; attempts and low-degree persons deliberately get no standalone HTML pages
- FORRT-compatible identity at the edge: doi_hash3 equals FLoRA's doi_o_hash for all 2,815 rows (tested), so /api/v1/doi/{hash3}.json works with FORRT's Zotero plugin and contribute-back is a column projection
- Charts as Preact components rendered statically by Astro and hydrated only on the explorer page: one chart codebase, zero JS on 95% of pages, no D3/Chart.js bundle
- pipeline migrate --plan/--apply: migration is a command that prints the file-by-file plan, blocks on unplanned files, scrubs the 52 key-bearing files, writes the archive index and re-runs the secrets scan before finishing

## D6-visionary
(full: C:\Users\OMISTAJA\PsychologyReplication\_planning\designs\D6-visionary.md)

**Summary:** D6 visionary design: 48 ranked ideas grounded in verified local data, a top-12 build order, a homepage concept ("The Record, today"), five candidate names with WebSearch collision checks, and an appendix of every number computed this session. Thesis: FORRT owns the rows, nobody owns the stories — make each effect a biography (claim sentence → fame → trial via three lenses → multi-criterion verdict → afterlife). Key verified assets: counts_by_year for 1,583 originals (Bargh 1996 still 148 cites in 2020, eight years after Doyen 2012; Kidd & Castano peaks 2018 after Panero 2016 failed); 1,148 internal citation edges with 263 pointing at failed originals (Mani 2013 scarcity cited by 32 other FReD originals); 733 FReD rows with r on both sides, median shrinkage ratio 0.58, 46% shrink by more than half; 2,131 literal claim sentences (claim_text_o) and 100% outcome_quote coverage in FLoRA; FLoRA journal rates with denominators (Psych Sci 224 attempts/28% successful, JPSP 151/29%, JCR 38/18%); independence 62% of attempts, independent success 41% vs 52%; p<=.005 52% vs .005-.05 37%; docx famous effects with GS fame (Pygmalion 13,625 not replicated; ego depletion 7,141). Name collisions found: "Holds Up" (holdsup.app, podcast fact-checker), "Second Look" (AI-safety replications), "Replication Record/Database" (FORRT's paper); "Retested", "Twice", "The Rerun" showed no collisions. Risks flagged: docx statuses are a 2021 snapshot, citation-outcome labels derive from legacy result column, counts_by_year covers 2012-2025 only, shared-state features need Supabase.

**Top ideas:**
- Claim-sentence vs outcome-quote as the atomic unit (2,131 literal original claims face-to-face with 100%-coverage FLoRA replication quotes), each stamped with a 'replication weather' glyph that doubles as badge, favicon, OG image and game card
- Calibration game with probability slider, Brier scoring, progressive cue reveal (p-bucket 52% vs 37%, N, prereg, journal base rate, independence) and a three-lens reveal ending on the citation curve; daily 'Replicle' mode
- Rise & Fall pages: citation curves for 1,583 originals with replication attempts as coloured markers, showing the field kept citing Bargh 1996 (148 cites in 2020) and Kidd & Castano (peak 2018) after they failed
- The Graveyard and The Survivors: typeset editorial front doors of famous failed (Pygmalion 13,625 GS cites, ego depletion 7,141) and famous surviving effects (anchoring 46k), each failed effect with its replication quote as epitaph
- Seven-criteria disagreement matrix for the 1,056 r-convertible rows plus a seeded power / small-telescopes / prediction-interval calculator on every effect page
- Built on a Failed Foundation: dependency graph from 1,148 internal citation edges, 263 of which point at failed originals (Mani 2013 scarcity cited by 32 later FReD originals)
- Web reference-list checker + bookmarklet + embeddable SVG badge, static and FORRT-API-compatible, so the replication record follows papers across the open web
- Predictors-of-replication dashboard recomputed every build with denominators (p-value bucket, independence 41% vs 52%, prereg, N, decade, discipline, interaction flag)
- Leaderboards with denominators: most-cited unreplicated, biggest shrinkage (median ratio 0.58, 46% halve), journals (Psych Sci 224/28%, JCR 38/18%), independence ledger
- Public review queue on each effect page fed by OpenAlex cites:<original>, weekly 'this week in replication' diff/RSS, follow-an-effect, Wanted list with crowd forecasts, and a 'what your textbook still teaches' OpenStax/Noba table
